questions.q: What architecture pattern is this phase explicitly NOT building?
options: A single-cloud deployment with no backup at all
An active-active architecture where both Azure and AWS take live customer traffic at once
A Kubernetes cluster of any kind
A primary/backup-DR architecture
questions.explain: Active-active across clouds roughly doubles operational surface area for a benefit Driftwood doesn't need yet — this phase keeps one cloud primary and the other as backup/DR.

questions.q: Which cloud is chosen as primary for the AKS migration, and why?
options: AWS, because it's cheaper
Azure, because identity, networking, and the existing managed databases these services depend on are already Azure-native
Azure, because AWS doesn't support Kubernetes
Neither — both clouds run the workload equally
questions.explain: Driftwood's Azure AD tenant, VNet, DNS, and the catalog/order databases from the intermediate project are already on Azure, so running the primary cluster there keeps compute next to data and identity.

questions.q: What role does AWS play in the target architecture, and what established pattern does that build on?
options: AWS runs a second, equally-live Kubernetes cluster
AWS remains the backup/DR target — cross-region-replicated object storage and a standby database replica, idle under normal operation — extending the pattern established in the intermediate project
AWS is dropped entirely in this phase
AWS becomes the new primary cloud, replacing Azure
questions.explain: AWS keeps the backup/DR role it already had from the intermediate project rather than the two clouds swapping roles or both running live traffic.

questions.q: Which direction does data flow between the two clouds under normal operation?
options: Bidirectionally, with both clouds writing to each other constantly
One direction only — from the live Azure primary to the AWS backup via async replication
From AWS to Azure, since AWS is primary
Data never leaves Azure under any circumstance
questions.explain: Azure is live and AWS receives replicated data and otherwise sits idle; the failover path only matters if Azure becomes unavailable.

questions.q: What is explicitly left undecided by this lesson's architecture diagram?
options: Which cloud is primary
How the AKS cluster itself is built (node pools, zones, scaling), how Terraform enforces this architecture across both clouds, and how cost/capacity gets reported — left to Lessons 4, 6, and 7
Whether AWS is involved at all
The names of the three services being migrated
questions.explain: This lesson settles which cloud runs what; the cluster build-out, the Terraform codification, and the FinOps reporting are each handled in later lessons.
